what: An R-package to gather bibliographic data from PubMed.
title: pubmedR: A brief example
text: https://massimoaria.github.io/pubmedR/ https://github.com/massimoaria/pubmedR Latest version: 1.0.2.9000, 2026-11-05   Massimo Aria Full Professor Social Statistics PhD Computational Statistics Laboratory Research Group STAD Statistics, Technology, Data Analysis Department Economics Statistics University Naples Federico II email aria@unina.https://www.massimoaria.com
code: The goal of pubmedR is to gather metadata about publications, grants and clinical trials from the PubMed database using NCBI REST APIs.

title: pubmedR: A brief example
text: can install development version pubmedR GitHub : can install released version pubmedR CRAN :
code: install.packages("devtools") devtools::install_github("massimoaria/pubmedR") install.packages("pubmedR")

title: pubmedR: A brief example
code: library(pubmedR)

title: pubmedR: A brief example
text: default, access NCBI API free strictly require API key. Without key, NCBI limits users 3 requests per second; registered users API key allowed 10 requests per second. obtain key, register “ncbi account” (https://account.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/) generate one “account settings page” (https://account.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/settings/). can pass key explicitly via api_key argument function, - preferably - set environment variable. pubmedR automatically pick PUBMED_API_KEY ENTREZ_KEY:
code: # option 1: pass it explicitly api_key <- "your API key"  # option 2: set it once per session (or in ~/.Renviron) Sys.setenv(PUBMED_API_KEY = "your API key")  # no key api_key <- NULL

title: pubmedR: A brief example
text: Imagine want download metadata collection journal articles (1) use bibliometric approaches, (2) published last two decades, (3) written English. Since version 0.1.0, pubmedR offers two equivalent workflows: step--step workflow (pmQueryBuild → pmQueryTotalCount → pmApiRequest → pmApi2df), gives full control stage; one-step workflow via pmCollect(), convenience wrapper chains whole pipeline single call optionally enriches result citation data.

title: pubmedR: A brief example
text: use cases, pmCollect() fastest way go query bibliometrix-ready data frame. builds query, checks total count, downloads records, converts XML data frame, (optionally) adds citation counts cited references. can also pass raw PubMed query string directly: Set enrich = TRUE add citation counts (TC) cited references (CR) via pmEnrichCitations(). also looks every cited PMID, takes longer large collections:
code: library(pubmedR)  M <- pmCollect(   terms      = "bibliometric*",   fields     = "Title/Abstract",   language   = "english",   pub_type   = "Journal Article",   date_range = c("2000", "2020"),   limit      = 2000,   api_key    = NULL )  # Query:  bibliometric*[Title/Abstract] AND english[LA] AND #         Journal Article[PT] AND 2000:2020[DP] # # Total records found: 3744 # Records to download: 2000 M <- pmCollect(   query   = "bibliometric*[Title/Abstract] AND english[LA] AND 2023:2024[DP]",   limit   = 200 ) M <- pmCollect(   terms      = "bibliometric*",   date_range = c("2023", "2024"),   limit      = 50,   enrich     = TRUE )

title: pubmedR: A brief example
text: prefer fine-grained control - example inspect translated query downloading - can run pipeline one stage time.

title: pubmedR: A brief example
text: Instead writing Entrez query string hand, can use pmQueryBuild() compose programmatically parameters: Several values language pub_type combined , language = c("english", "italian"). course, can still write query manually prefer:
code: query <- pmQueryBuild(   terms      = "bibliometric*",   fields     = "Title/Abstract",   language   = "english",   pub_type   = "Journal Article",   date_range = c("2000", "2020") )  query # [1] "bibliometric*[Title/Abstract] AND english[LA] AND #      Journal Article[PT] AND 2000:2020[DP]" query <- "bibliometric*[Title/Abstract] AND english[LA] AND Journal Article[PT] AND 2000:2020[DP]"

what: Step 2: Check the effectiveness of the query
title: pubmedR: A brief example
text: Use pmQueryTotalCount() see many records PubMed return, along automatically translated query: pmCountByYear() shows records spread years, without downloading :
code: res <- pmQueryTotalCount(query = query, api_key = api_key)  res$total_count # [1] 3744  res$query_translation # [1] "\"bibliometric*\"[Title/Abstract] AND \"english\"[Language] AND #      \"journal article\"[Publication Type] AND #      2000/01/01:2020/12/31[Date - Publication]" pmCountByYear(query, years = 2018:2020) #   year count # 1 2018   482 # 2 2019   636 # 3 2020  1004

what: Step 3: Download the collection of document metadata
title: pubmedR: A brief example
text: can now download whole collection (subset, lowering limit): PubMed serves 9,999 records per search. ask , pmApiRequest() splits query date records added PubMed downloads parts turn. records come order, newest first, order original search. pmApiRequest() returns list following elements: data - XML-structured list containing bibliographic metadata collection downloaded PubMed. query - original query submitted user. query_translation - query translated executed NCBI’s Automatic Terms Translation system. records_downloaded - number records actually downloaded. total_count - total number records matching query.
code: D <- pmApiRequest(query = query, limit = res$total_count, api_key = api_key)

what: Step 4: Convert the XML object into a data frame
title: pubmedR: A brief example
text: Finally, transform XML-structured object D data frame rows documents columns field tags compatible bibliometrix R package (https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=bibliometrix, https://bibliometrix.org/). Setting format = "raw" keeps field tags, text PubMed writes rather upper case, leaves AU_CO AU1_CO. Three fields worth closer look: PY year journal issue. [DP] tag query also matches electronic publication date, query can return documents later PY: article online 2020 issue 2021 matches 2000:2020[DP], PY 2021. applies 163 3,744 documents. DT holds first publication type, usually “Journal Article” even review. PT holds : AU also lists collective authors, place among others, count authors analyses.
code: M <- pmApi2df(D, format = "bibliometrix")  dim(M) # [1] 3744   33  names(M) #  [1] "AU"        "AF"        "TI"        "SO"        "SO_CO"     "LA" #  [7] "DT"        "PT"        "DE"        "ID"        "MESH"      "AB" # [13] "C1"        "CR"        "TC"        "SN"        "J9"        "JI" # [19] "PY"        "PY_IS"     "VL"        "IS"        "DI"        "PG" # [25] "GRANT_ID"  "GRANT_ORG" "UT"        "PMID"      "PMCID"     "DB" # [31] "AU_UN"     "AU_CO"     "AU1_CO" sum(grepl("REVIEW", M$PT))   # [1] 862

what: Fetching records by PMID or DOI
title: pubmedR: A brief example
text: already know articles want, can bypass query step download records directly PubMed identifiers pmFetchById(): pmFetchByDoi() DOIs, instance complete collection another database, lists DOIs PubMed: return structure pmApiRequest(), result can fed pmApi2df() exactly way.
code: pmids <- c("34813985", "34813456", "34812345") D <- pmFetchById(pmids = pmids, api_key = api_key) M <- pmApi2df(D) D <- pmFetchByDoi(c("10.1038/nature14539", "10.9999/not.a.real.doi")) D$not_found # [1] "10.9999/not.a.real.doi"

title: pubmedR: A brief example
text: PubMed records carry citation count, TC 0 download. two sources : pmCitedBy(pmid) returns PMIDs articles citing given article. come NCBI’s E-Link service, counts citing articles PubMed Central. pmICite(pmids) returns citation counts Relative Citation Ratio NIH iCite, built larger NIH Open Citation Collection. API key needed. counts can differ widely: cited references: pmExtractReferences(D) returns one row per reference records already downloaded, requests; pmReferences(pmid) returns PMIDs referenced one article, E-Link, works articles full text PubMed Central. pmEnrichCitations() adds TC, CR (cited references) NR (number) whole data frame. Pass downloaded records P avoid fetching , choose source counts tc_source: article whose count retrieved keeps TC, warning. Note: citation data PubMed Central less comprehensive commercial databases Web Science Scopus.
code: pmCitedBy(pmid = "25824007")$count # [1] 31  pmICite("25824007")[, c("pmid", "citation_count", "relative_citation_ratio")] #       pmid citation_count relative_citation_ratio # 1 25824007             40                1.517149 M_enriched <- pmEnrichCitations(M, P = D, tc_source = "icite", api_key = api_key)

what: An overview of the collection using bibliometrix
title: pubmedR: A brief example
text: data frame M, can use bibliometrix descriptive network analyses (https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=bibliometrix, https://bibliometrix.org/). can also work Biblioshiny app, can download PubMed :
code: install.packages("bibliometrix") library(bibliometrix)  M <- convert2df(D, dbsource = "pubmed", format = "api") results <- biblioAnalysis(M) summary(results, k = 10)  # Main Information about data # #  Timespan                              2000:2024 #  Sources (Journals, Books, etc)        1525 #  Documents                             3744 #  ... biblioshiny()

title: Gathering Metadata About Publications, Grants, Clinical Trials from PubMed Database
text: pubmedR downloads bibliographic records PubMed NCBI API turns data frame ready analysis R. data frame uses field tags bibliometrix, can pass straight package Biblioshiny app.

title: Gathering Metadata About Publications, Grants, Clinical Trials from PubMed Database
text: API free needs key. Without one, NCBI allows 3 requests per second; free API key allows 10. use key every session, add PUBMED_API_KEY=your_key .Renviron file (usethis::edit_r_environ() opens ).
code: # The released version, from CRAN install.packages("pubmedR")  # The development version, from GitHub # install.packages("remotes") remotes::install_github("massimoaria/pubmedR")

title: Gathering Metadata About Publications, Grants, Clinical Trials from PubMed Database
text: pmCollect() builds query, downloads records converts one call:
code: library(pubmedR)  M <- pmCollect(   terms = "bibliometric*",   language = "english",   pub_type = "Review",   date_range = c("2020", "2024"),   limit = 5 ) knitr::kable(M[, c("PY", "TI", "SO")], row.names = FALSE)

title: Gathering Metadata About Publications, Grants, Clinical Trials from PubMed Database
text: control, run step . pmQueryBuild() writes query, can write PubMed search syntax: Check many records finds downloading , see spread years: download records convert : PubMed serves 9,999 records per search. ask , pmApiRequest() splits query date records added PubMed downloads parts turn. records come order, newest first, order original search.
code: query <- pmQueryBuild(   terms = c("machine learning", "deep learning"),   operator = "OR",   mesh_terms = "Neoplasms",   language = c("english", "italian"),   date_range = c("2022", "2024") ) query #> [1] "(machine learning[Title/Abstract] OR deep learning[Title/Abstract]) AND Neoplasms[MeSH Terms] AND (english[LA] OR italian[LA]) AND 2022:2024[DP]" pmQueryTotalCount(query)$total_count #> [1] 12119  pmCountByYear(query, years = 2022:2024) #>   year count #> 1 2022  3378 #> 2 2023  4081 #> 3 2024  5699 D <- pmApiRequest(query, limit = 20) M <- pmApi2df(D) dim(M) #> [1] 20 33

title: Gathering Metadata About Publications, Grants, Clinical Trials from PubMed Database
text: Download records PMID DOI. pmFetchByDoi() also tells DOIs PubMed:
code: by_pmid <- pmFetchById(c("10171110", "25824007"))  known <- pmApi2df(by_pmid)  by_doi <- pmFetchByDoi(c("10.1038/nature14539", "10.9999/not.a.real.doi")) knitr::kable(known[, c("PMID", "PY", "TI")], row.names = FALSE) by_doi$not_found #> [1] "10.9999/not.a.real.doi"

title: Gathering Metadata About Publications, Grants, Clinical Trials from PubMed Database
text: PubMed records carry citation count, TC 0 download. two sources .
